meta.scene_summary: We've successfully automated the process of setting our own money on fire.

cooking.headline: Cisco is letting an engineer speedrun their legacy code with AI
cooking.summary: They handed one dev unlimited AI tokens and told him to rewrite 98% of the company's legacy codebase in two years. It's essentially the corporate version of being given a blank check to replace the foundation of a house while the family is still eating dinner inside.
cooking.plain_english: Cisco has authorized a software engineer to use unlimited artificial intelligence resources to modernize nearly all of the company's existing code within a two-year timeframe.

cooking.headline: A new Linux TCP vulnerability just dropped, as if your production uptime wasn't already a fragile miracle.
cooking.summary: The Linux kernel has a new use-after-free vulnerability in the TCP stack, reminding us that the internet is held together by duct tape and prayers. It's the perfect time to patch your servers and pray you didn't accidentally break the one library your entire legacy stack depends on.
cooking.plain_english: A new security vulnerability has been discovered in the Linux kernel's TCP network communication code that requires a software patch.

cooked.headline: Binance just had a $5.6B 'oops' moment
cooked.summary: Losing billions in a hack is a bold way to prove your security is essentially just a suggestion. At this point, keeping your crypto on an exchange is basically leaving your wallet on a park bench and hoping for the best.
cooked.plain_english: Binance suffered a massive security breach resulting in the theft of 5.6 billion dollars worth of assets.

cooked.headline: Intel's stock just performed a successful skydive without a parachute
cooked.summary: Intel's outlook is so grim that the stock market decided to start the holiday sale season a few months early. It turns out that being the backbone of the PC industry doesn't help much when nobody is buying the PCs.
cooked.plain_english: Intel's stock price dropped by 25 percent following a negative financial forecast and concerns regarding the company's future performance.

cooked.headline: Google just evaporated $500B because the AI hype train hit a speed bump
cooked.summary: Wall Street spent years betting that Google would own the AI future, only to panic the moment the math didn't look like a straight line to the moon. It turns out that when you build a trillion-dollar company on vibes, the stock price is just a group project where everyone forgets to do the homework on time.
cooked.plain_english: Google's market value dropped by $500 billion following investor concerns about the company's performance and strategy in the artificial intelligence sector.

cooked.headline: Azure's security is basically a shared Netflix account for your entire cloud infrastructure
cooked.summary: Researchers found five ways to jump between tenants, proving that Azure's walls are more like suggestions written on a whiteboard. It's comforting to know that even when you pay for enterprise cloud, your data is still essentially playing a high-stakes game of hot potato with every other company on the server.
cooked.plain_english: Security researchers identified five vulnerabilities in Microsoft Azure that allowed unauthorized access across different customer environments.

cooked.headline: Claude Code extensions are now effectively a 'bring your own backdoor' party
cooked.summary: Anthropic's official tools were found to be vulnerable to supply chain attacks, turning your AI coding assistant into an unwanted remote worker. It turns out that letting an AI write your code is risky, but letting the extension write it for you while someone else watches is a whole new level of 'oops'.
cooked.plain_english: Hackers discovered security vulnerabilities in official software extensions used for Claude, potentially allowing unauthorized access to user systems.

cooked.headline: Northflank got breached, proving that even the cloud isn't just someone else's computer—it's someone else's problem
cooked.summary: The platform that promises to make hosting easy has had a security incident, reminding us all that 'managed services' is just a fancy term for 'we'll handle the breach for you'. At least now you have a great excuse for why your staging environment is currently unreachable.
cooked.plain_english: The cloud computing provider Northflank experienced a security breach that compromised their systems.

cooked.headline: Betting on the market is fun until the vendor gets phished
cooked.summary: Polymarket had to hit the pause button because a vendor compromise turned their security into a suggestion. It turns out even a platform built on predicting the future couldn't see their own account takeover coming.
cooked.plain_english: Polymarket temporarily halted trading because an outside service provider was compromised, leading to unauthorized access to some user wallets.

cooked.headline: Proton CEO says they're done hiring engineers, which is a bold strategy for a tech company.
cooked.summary: Proton is betting that AI can replace the entire engineering team, finally solving the age-old problem of having to manage actual human beings. It's a bold move to fire your workforce before the robots have even figured out how to fix a merge conflict without crying.
cooked.plain_english: The CEO of Proton stated that the company will stop hiring new engineers, likely due to the increasing efficiency of artificial intelligence in software development.
